editorial:
Imagine you are a proud cowboy who loves the open range, but suddenly, the world changes around you. That is exactly where you find yourself with Monte Walsh. You get to follow an older cowboy who is realizing that the age of the free range is over. Barbed wire fences are popping up everywhere, and the trains are taking over the land. It is a slow-burn story that feels more like a sad goodbye than a loud action flick. You will feel the weight of the world on Monte's shoulders as he and his buddies try to figure out where they fit in a world that does not want them anymore.

What really works here is the acting, which feels grounded and real. You will love how the movie focuses on the friendship between the men rather than just gunfights. While the pacing is a bit slow for some, it helps you feel the loneliness of the prairie. If you enjoy stories about old heroes facing hard times, you should definitely check this one out.
endingExplained: In the end, Monte realizes that he cannot fight the change of the times. After dealing with the conflicts involving the land and the local people, he has to accept that the era of the wandering cowboy is dead. He says a final, sad goodbye to the lifestyle he loved. Instead of fighting a losing battle, he decides to move forward and try to find a new way to live in a modern world.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about old-school heroes and the death of the Wild West.
